newsitem.title: ITALY: Norwegian sets out on solo Antarctic trek.
newsitem.headline: Norwegian sets out on solo Antarctic trek.

text.p: Norwegian explorer Borge Ousland on Friday launched his second attempt to trek nearly 3,000 km (1,800 miles) across the Antarctic continent alone and unsupported, his sponsor said.
"A signal transmitted via satellite at 0300 GMT this morning confirmed that Ousland had begun his journey," the sponsor said in a statement issued from its Milan public relations office.
"Setting out from Berkner Island in the Weddel Sea, Ousland faces the longest single-handed ski trek ever made: 2,700 km (1,700 miles) to reach the Mcmurdo Base on Ross Island via the South Pole."
During a first attempt at the route last year, the Norwegian reached the South Pole but was forced by frostbite to give up after 44 days in the world's coldest continent.
At that time Ousland was racing explorer Roger Mear to set a new endurance record, but the Briton also had to abandon his trek after vital equipment failed.
Ousland sponsors claimed he was "the first man in the world who can claim to have made solo expeditions to both of the Earth's poles without external support".
